praepĭlo , no
I.perf., ātum, 1, v. a. praepilum, to point in front or at the end like a pilum (post-class.): praepilatis missilibus principiis pugnae tentatis, Amm. 24, 6, 10 —
II. To throw forwards, hurl before (postclass.): “praepilabantur missilia,” Amm. 16, 12, 36 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
